door-installation-princeton: Doors in Princeton's older houses have been settling for a very long time, so a new door has to be fitted to the opening that exists, not the one on the label. We plane, shim, and tune interior and exterior doors around the Western Section, Riverside, and the streets off Nassau, replace hollow-core slabs in the 1960s ranches in Littlebrook, and add deadbolts and keypad locks while the tools are out.
door-installation-west-windsor: The 1990s colonials around Princeton Junction and Dutch Neck came with builder-grade six-panel doors that never closed quite right and are now twenty-five years worse. We swap them in the same opening, fit new entry and storm doors so there is no daylight around the frame, and get the bifolds in the bedrooms back on their tracks, all in one trip.
door-installation-plainsboro: Plainsboro townhomes in Princeton Collection, Ravens Crest, and Hunters Glen run on bifold closets, sliding patio doors, and hollow-core bedroom doors that have seen a few owners. We re-track, replace, and adjust them inside the unit, and fit a new entry door or storm door where the association allows it.
door-installation-lawrence-township: Lawrence gives us both ends of the door trade: prewar frames in Lawrenceville village that need a door fitted rather than just hung, and 1980s and 90s frames off Princeton Pike where a prehung swap is the quick answer. Either way we finish with weatherstripping that seals and hardware that turns with two fingers.
door-installation-montgomery: Entry doors on Montgomery's open lots in Skillman and Belle Mead take wind and weather with nothing to block them, so seals, sweeps, and thresholds matter more here than in a townhome. We install and adjust entry, storm, and interior doors across the township and match the heavier millwork in the newer custom homes.
door-installation-pennington: Pennington Borough doors are mostly old, wood, and worth keeping, so we start by asking whether the door needs replacing or just tuning. We plane and rehang the originals along Main Street where they are sound, replace them in the same opening where they are not, and handle the standard swaps in Brookside and the Hopewell Township streets nearby.
door-installation-south-brunswick: Kendall Park's 1950s and 60s ranches and splits still have a lot of their original interior doors, and many are painted shut or hanging on stripped hinges. We replace and adjust doors across South Brunswick, from those older streets to the newer subdivisions in Dayton and Monmouth Junction, with proper shimming and hardware that works from day one.
door-installation-cranbury: Cranbury's village houses on Main Street and Maplewood Avenue have doors that were hung by hand generations ago, and they deserve to be tuned by hand rather than swapped for a big-box slab. We adjust and repair the originals, and on the newer properties out Cranbury Neck and Old Trenton Road we install entry, storm, and interior doors the standard way.
door-installation-east-windsor: Twin Rivers townhomes are past fifty years old and the doors show it: bifolds off the track, hollow-core bedroom doors with the veneer lifting, entry doors that leak air. We handle the whole list in one visit, and we do the same in the Hickory Acres and Princeton Manor colonials, where the entry and storm doors tend to be the first thing to go.
door-installation-robbinsville: Robbinsville's houses are young enough that the frames are still square, which makes door work quick: slabs and prehungs go in clean, and most of what we see is builder hardware wearing out. We swap knobs, deadbolts, and keypad locks, re-track closet doors in the Town Center and Foxmoor townhomes, and replace entry doors in the same opening.
drywall-repair-princeton: Half the walls in Princeton's older houses are plaster, not drywall, and patching one like the other is how you end up with a bump that shows in every light. We repair plaster as plaster in the Western Section and around Nassau Street, patch and texture drywall in the Riverside and Littlebrook ranches, and prime everything so the repair does not flash through the paint.
drywall-repair-west-windsor: West Windsor's 1990s colonials crack in the same places: the corners above windows and doors, and along the seams in tall foyer ceilings. We tape those with mesh and setting compound so they stay closed, patch doorknob holes and anchor damage, and replace water-stained board after the leak is fixed, from Princeton Junction to Grovers Mill.
drywall-repair-plainsboro: Townhome drywall in Plainsboro has usually been patched a few times by previous owners, and not always well. We cut out the bad work in Princeton Collection, Ravens Crest, and Fox Run units, tape and feather properly, match the texture, and leave it primed. Water stains on a ceiling get a straight answer about where the water came from.
drywall-repair-lawrence-township: Lawrence Township mixes plaster in the Lawrenceville village houses with drywall in Eldridge Park, Slackwood, and the newer streets off Princeton Pike. We know which is which on sight and repair each with the right materials, feathering patches wide and matching texture so the fix disappears once it is painted.
drywall-repair-montgomery: Montgomery's newer homes in Skillman and Belle Mead have tall ceilings and long unbroken walls where a patch has nowhere to hide, so we feather wide and prime before paint. Nail pops, settling cracks, and damage from a moved TV mount are the usual calls, along with ceiling repairs after a bathroom or roof leak has been fixed.
drywall-repair-pennington: Pennington Borough walls along Main Street are often plaster over lath, which cracks differently and needs a different repair than drywall. We patch plaster properly, repair drywall in the Brookside and Hopewell Township streets, and match textures so the repair is not visible under paint.
drywall-repair-south-brunswick: Kendall Park's older ranches and splits have drywall that has been through sixty years of hanging pictures and a few remodels, while Dayton and Monmouth Junction homes crack along the window corners and ceiling seams as they settle. We repair both across South Brunswick and prime every patch so it does not flash.
drywall-repair-cranbury: Cranbury's historic village houses are plaster and horsehair in places, and we treat them accordingly: no drywall screws into old lath, no quick-set over a crack that needs to be keyed in. Newer homes toward Cranbury Neck get standard drywall patching, texture matching, and priming.
drywall-repair-east-windsor: Twin Rivers units have fifty years of drywall repairs in them, some good and some not. We cut out the failed patches, retape, and blend so the wall reads as one surface, and we do the same in the Hickory Acres and Princeton Manor colonials. Water-damaged board comes out rather than getting painted over.
drywall-repair-robbinsville: Robbinsville drywall is newer, which means the damage is mostly life, not age: doorknob holes, anchors pulled out by a fallen shelf, cracks at the corners as the house finishes settling. We patch, texture, and prime across Town Center, Foxmoor, and the Route 33 subdivisions, and most lists fit inside one $345 visit.
deck-staining-princeton: Princeton decks off the Riverside and Littlebrook ranches are shaded by mature trees, which means mildew and moss more than sun fade. We wash thoroughly, let the wood dry, replace the soft boards, and stain during a dry stretch. In the Western Section we treat wood porches the same way, with finishes that suit the age of the house.
deck-staining-west-windsor: West Windsor decks were mostly built with the houses in the 1990s and have gone too long between coats. We wash, sand the rough spots, swap any punky boards, tighten the railings, and stain on a dry weather window across Princeton Junction, Dutch Neck, and Grovers Mill. Every two to three years and the deck outlives the mortgage.
deck-staining-plainsboro: Plainsboro's single-family homes have decks that need the standard restore: wash, dry, repair, stain. In the townhome communities the association usually owns the exterior, so ask your HOA first; where decks belong to the unit, we treat them like any other deck and schedule around the forecast, not the calendar.
deck-staining-lawrence-township: Decks in Lawrence Township's newer neighborhoods off Princeton Pike and Franklin Corner Road are hitting the age where the sealer is long gone and the boards are graying. We bring them back with a proper wash, board replacement where needed, and stain applied to dry wood. Older porches in Lawrenceville village get the same care with period-appropriate finishes.
deck-staining-montgomery: Montgomery's large-lot decks in Skillman and Belle Mead get full sun and full wind, so they weather faster than a shaded townhome deck. We wash, replace the boards that have split, tighten the rails, and stain with a product suited to the exposure. Bigger decks and pool decks get one written price for the whole job.
deck-staining-pennington: Pennington decks and porches, from Brookside back yards to Main Street porches, get the same sequence: wash, dry, repair, stain. We schedule around a dry stretch of weather because stain on damp wood fails early, and we replace the soft boards first so the finish is not just painting over a problem.
deck-staining-south-brunswick: South Brunswick decks in Dayton and Monmouth Junction are twenty to thirty years old and often on their first restain ever. We wash off the gray, sand, replace cracked boards, tighten railings, and stain across the township, including the older Kendall Park decks that need a few more boards than most.
deck-staining-cranbury: Cranbury decks range from small village back yards to larger decks on the Cranbury Neck properties. We prep properly, replace what is soft, and stain with the right product for the wood and the exposure. Spring and fall fill up fast, so book ahead.
deck-staining-east-windsor: Decks on East Windsor's single-family streets in Hickory Acres and Princeton Manor are due, and many of the older ones need boards and a railing fix before stain goes on. We fold repair, wash, and stain into one job with one written price. Twin Rivers exterior work belongs to the association in most cases, so check there first.
deck-staining-robbinsville: Robbinsville decks are newer but were often left bare since the day the builder finished, so the first coat of stain is overdue. We wash, sand, and stain across Foxmoor, Sharon, and the subdivisions along Route 33, with a repair-versus-replace opinion on any boards that have cupped or split.
fence-repair-princeton: Princeton fences lean, sag, and rot like everyone else's, plus a share of older picket and split-rail fences in the Western Section that need parts made rather than bought. We reset posts, replace pickets and panels, and rehang gates across town, matching what is there rather than selling you a new fence.
fence-repair-west-windsor: West Windsor's privacy and picket fences went in with the houses in the 1990s, and the posts are the weak point: clay soil, freeze-thaw, and thirty winters. We dig out and reset leaning posts in concrete, replace the rotted ones, swap panels, and rehang gates so they latch, from Princeton Junction to Penns Neck.
fence-repair-plainsboro: Fence repair for Plainsboro's single-family homes: posts reset, panels and pickets replaced, gates fixed so they close. In the townhome communities fences are usually the association's responsibility, so check with your HOA; where they are yours, we repair rather than replace and match the existing style.
fence-repair-lawrence-township: Lawrence Township fences are a mix of chain-link and wood on the older streets in Eldridge Park and Slackwood and privacy fence in the newer neighborhoods off Princeton Pike. We reset leaning posts, replace broken pickets and rails, fix chain-link, and rebuild gates so they swing and latch cleanly.
fence-repair-montgomery: Montgomery's open lots take wind that a townhome fence never sees, and a stretch of privacy fence in Skillman or Belle Mead can go over in a single storm. We reset and replace posts, rebuild damaged sections, and rehang gates with hardware that will not rust out in two seasons. Split-rail and paddock fence repairs too.
fence-repair-pennington: Pennington fence work runs from picket repairs on Main Street, where style has to fit the house, to standard wood and vinyl fence repairs in Brookside and the surrounding Hopewell Township streets. Gate sag, post rot, and broken panels are the usual calls, and we match the existing fence so the repair does not advertise itself.
fence-repair-south-brunswick: South Brunswick fences in Kendall Park are often more patch than fence by now, and the newer privacy fences in Dayton and Monmouth Junction are failing at the posts. We tell you honestly what is worth saving, reset or replace the posts, swap panels and pickets, and rehang gates with latches that catch.
fence-repair-cranbury: Cranbury fence repair covers the village's picket and split-rail fences, which need parts that suit the period, and the wood and vinyl fences on the newer properties toward Cranbury Neck. Post resets, panel swaps, and gate rebuilds are the bread and butter, with a straight opinion when a section is past saving.
fence-repair-east-windsor: Fences on East Windsor's single-family streets in Hickory Acres and Princeton Manor take the same beating as everyone's: heaved posts, rotted bottoms, gates that drag. We reset posts, replace boards and panels, and rehang gates. In Twin Rivers the association handles most fencing, so ask them before booking.
fence-repair-robbinsville: Robbinsville fences are newer, so the repairs are usually storm damage and gate hardware rather than rot: a panel blown out, a gate that sags because the hinges were never right. We fix what broke, brace the gate, and match the existing fence across Foxmoor, Sharon, and the Route 33 subdivisions.
